correctness.rationale: Starting from the directional stationary equations, mass/polarization summation gives S'=-r rho and R'=-(r+alpha)sigma. The phase invariant, its vanishing from far-field decay and interface transmission, and positivity of outward current force sigma=q rho with q=sqrt(r/(r+alpha)). Thus F'(rho)rho'=-Gamma rho throughout, exactly imposing the normalized source jump. Strictly monotone inverse-flux integrals construct unique branches and masses, and the gas tail is infinite because F_g'(0)>0. The sharp unique optimizer of cp u^p follows by exact differentiation; all boundaries, positivity and p endpoints checked. Standalone independent-function numerical tests passed 570 scalar assertions, but proof is analytical.

value.rationale: The gas-independent core width, mass and central density give a whole-function invariance under changes of dilute-gas motility at fixed contact flux, directly testing phase geometry in resetting active matter. The previously known constant-speed core has normalized optimal Gamma ratio e, whereas decreasing dense speeds yield a continuous, strictly ordered spectrum from 1 to e (e.g. ratio 2 for a square-root core flux). This is a motivated physical control classification and not a numeric slice or table recomputation.
